_description: Gold dataset for E1-intake-extraction (app/evals/plan.py). Owner: Sham Goh. Scores SymptomIntakeAgent on the three fields it writes. THE POINT OF THIS FILE is that the two paths are scored SEPARATELY: the deterministic _fallback() is English-only by design and performs no translation, so scoring it on Chinese input would measure a documented decision as if it were a defect. Language detection is scored on every row (it is deterministic and language-independent); keyword metrics are scored on the rows each path is designed to handle, and the non-English deterministic result is reported as a coverage number rather than a pass/fail. Gold keywords were written from the patient text FIRST and only then compared against the extractor — where the two disagree, the gold stands and the test fails. That is the point of a gold set.

_schema.id: stable identifier, used in failure messages
_schema.text: raw patient input, exactly as a patient would type or dictate it
_schema.declared_language: what the UI sends in TriageRequest.language — deliberately WRONG or left at the 'en' default on some rows, because a real UI cannot be trusted
_schema.gold_language: the language the patient actually wrote in (ISO 639-1)
_schema.gold_keywords: the canonical keywords a clinician would expect to be extracted; drawn from intake._SYMPTOM_VOCABULARY labels
_schema.is_voice: true = arrived via speech-to-text, so it carries transcription noise
_schema.notes: why a triage nurse would label it this way
_schema.deterministic_expected: true = the deterministic _fallback() is expected to extract the gold keywords. False for ALL non-English rows (English-only vocabulary, no translation) and for the misspelling rows, which exist precisely to prove the empty-keyword LLM trigger is necessary. Keyword metrics for the fallback are scored on the true rows; the LLM path is scored on every row.

cases.text: I have crushing chest pain and I cannot breathe properly.
cases.notes: Textbook ACS wording. Both keywords are literal; anything less is a miss.

cases.text: I have had a bad cough and a fever for two days.
cases.notes: Common presentation. Duration is present but not itself a symptom keyword.

cases.text: My face is drooping on one side and my speech is slurred.
cases.notes: FAST signs. One canonical keyword covers both surface forms.

cases.text: I ate peanuts and now my throat is closing and my tongue is swelling.
cases.notes: Anaphylaxis. Must not be reported as sore throat — different urgency entirely.

cases.text: I have been thinking about suicide and I want to die.
cases.notes: Must be caught from 'suicide' as well as 'suicidal'.

cases.text: I have a deep cut on my arm and it will not stop bleeding.
cases.notes: 'will not stop bleeding' is the severity signal, not the cut itself.

cases.text: My son had a seizure this morning and was convulsing.
cases.notes: Third-party report; the symptom is still the patient's.

cases.text: Severe stomach pain and I keep vomiting since last night.
cases.notes: Two distinct signals. 'Severe' is deliberately NOT labelled as the separate 'severe pain' keyword: that entry means a GENERIC severity claim ('worst pain of my life'), and severity attached to a located pain is already carried by 'abdominal pain'. Emitting both would tell the clinician nothing extra.

cases.text: I feel really nauseous but I have not actually thrown up.
cases.notes: THE NAUSEA/VOMITING SEPARATION TEST. Reporting 'vomiting' here asserts a symptom the patient explicitly denied — a hallucination, not a near-miss.

cases.text: I twisted my ankle playing football and it is bruised.
cases.notes: Minor trauma — the category E5 found the model was blind to.

cases.text: Runny nose, blocked nose and sneezing since yesterday.
cases.notes: Three surface forms collapse to one canonical keyword; must not be reported three times.

cases.text: I feel dizzy and lightheaded with a bad headache.
cases.notes: Two separate canonical keywords.

cases.text: I have an itchy rash all over my arms.
cases.notes: Low acuity; included so the set is not all emergencies.

cases.text: My throat hurts when I swallow.
cases.notes: Must not be confused with the throat-swelling anaphylaxis wording.

cases.text: I am dehydrated and cannot keep fluids down.
cases.notes: Both surface forms map to one keyword.

cases.text: Chest pain, cannot breathe, throat swelling, heavy bleeding, a seizure, the worst pain of my life, fever and a cough.
cases.notes: THE TRUNCATION TEST. Eight symptoms, cap is six. Fever and cough are the two that may be dropped; dropping chest pain instead would be a safety failure.

cases.text: cant breath properly and my chest feels tight
cases.notes: MISSPELLED EMERGENCY. 'breath' is missing its final e, so the deterministic vocabulary cannot match it — this row is what the empty-keyword LLM trigger exists for. 'chest feels tight' is also not a literal vocabulary form.

cases.text: bad coff and hedache since yesterday
cases.notes: Two misspellings at once. Deterministic path is expected to score zero here; the LLM path must recover both.

cases.text: I have a feaver and my stomache hurts
cases.notes: Phonetic misspellings a stressed patient plausibly types.

cases.text: um  i uh i i have like a really bad  headache and um nausea
cases.notes: VOICE NOISE. Fillers and a stutter-repeat. 'like' must survive — 'feels like' is clinical description, not filler.

cases.text: so uh my chest has been hurting erm since this morning and you know i feel dizzy
cases.notes: 'chest has been hurting' is a paraphrase the literal vocabulary cannot match — only 'dizzy' is a literal hit. Recovering chest pain here needs the LLM.

cases.text: erm i have had a cough and a fever mm for a few days now
cases.notes: Voice noise around otherwise literal symptoms — the deterministic path must still get both.

cases.text: Tengo un dolor fuerte en el pecho y no puedo respirar
cases.notes: Spanish emergency, language correctly declared.

cases.text: Tengo fiebre y tos desde hace tres dias
cases.notes: WRONG DECLARATION. The UI says English; marker evidence must override it.

cases.text: Me duele mucho la cabeza
cases.notes: Short utterance — fewer markers, so detection is harder.

cases.text: Estoy vomitando y no puedo retener liquidos
cases.notes: Two signals in Spanish. NOTE: 'vomitando' is an accidental COGNATE hit — the English surface form 'vomit' prefix-matches it, so the deterministic path recovers one keyword here without translating. Unplanned but correct; measured by test_non_english_coverage_gap_is_quantified.

cases.text: Tengo dolor de garganta y me duele al tragar
cases.notes: Low-acuity Spanish case.

cases.text: 我胸口很痛，不能呼吸
cases.notes: Chinese emergency. Script detection must be exact.

cases.text: 我发烧和咳嗽三天了
cases.notes: WRONG DECLARATION plus non-Latin script — script must win over the declaration.

cases.text: 我头痛得很厉害
cases.notes: Short Chinese utterance.

cases.text: 我一直呕吐，没有胃口
cases.notes: Chinese, moderate acuity.

cases.text: 我喉咙痛，吞咽困难
cases.notes: Low-acuity Chinese case.

cases.text: Saya sakit dada dan susah bernafas
cases.notes: Malay emergency — a very likely real presentation in Singapore.

cases.text: Saya demam dan batuk sejak tiga hari
cases.notes: WRONG DECLARATION, Latin script — this one relies entirely on marker words.

cases.text: Kepala saya sakit sangat
cases.notes: Short Malay utterance.

cases.text: Saya muntah dan tidak boleh makan
cases.notes: Malay, moderate acuity.

cases.text: J'ai une douleur dans la poitrine et je ne peux pas respirer
cases.notes: French emergency.

cases.text: J'ai mal à la tête depuis trois jours
cases.notes: ACCENT FOLDING TEST — 'tête' must match the unaccented marker 'tete'.

cases.text: J'ai de la fièvre et une toux depuis hier
cases.notes: Accented French with two symptoms.

cases.text: எனக்கு நெஞ்சு வலி, மூச்சு விட முடியவில்லை
cases.notes: TAMIL EMERGENCY. One of Singapore's four official languages; the reason ta was added to _LANGUAGE_HINTS.

cases.text: எனக்கு காய்ச்சல் மற்றும் இருமல் இருக்கிறது
cases.notes: WRONG DECLARATION — Tamil script must override it, same as Chinese.

cases.text: எனக்கு கடுமையான தலைவலி
cases.notes: Short Tamil utterance.

cases.text: எனக்கு வயிற்று வலி மிகவும் அதிகமாக உள்ளது
cases.notes: Tamil, moderate acuity.

cases.text: எனக்கு தொண்டை வலி இருக்கிறது
cases.notes: Low-acuity Tamil case, so the set is not all emergencies.
